newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty condemns Russian security force "torture".
newsitem.headline: Amnesty condemns Russian security force "torture".

text.p: Amnesty International on Thursday condemned what it called widespread, systematic use of torture by Russia's security forces.
New, post-communist legislation and older Soviet-era laws both encourage abuses and go against international standards, the London-based human rights organisation said in a report.

"Under the guise of fighting crime, the Russian Federation has expanded the powers of security and law enforcement agencies to the detriment of constitutional rights, and members of ethnic minorities are particularly vulnerable," Amnesty said.
Amnesty said its report also described conditions of detention in Russia as "amounting to torture".
Amnesty said it had received reports that prisoners die from overcrowding, lack of oxygen and poor conditions.
Cases of death from lack of oxygen have taken place in almost all large pre-trial detention centres in Russia, Amnesty said.

It cited an example from July 1995, when 11 prisoners died of heat stroke in an overcrowded prison in Novokuznetsk in the Kemerovo region. Up to 25 people were being held in cells meant for 10 and the temperature rose as high as 48 to 51 Celsius (118 to 124 Fahrenheit). Amnesty said that ethnic minorities, such as Chechens and people from the Caucasus, were particularly vulnerable while in police custody.

The report also documents the use of torture and ill-treatment by both sides of the armed conflict in Chechnya, including the use of electric shock torture, rape as a form of punishment against residents of villages believed to support Chechen fighters, hostage taking and possible extra-judicial executions.
Amnesty added: "It is clearly within the power of the Russian authorities to eliminate these illegal practices."
